key_insight: RadKev is an open-weight decision model specialized for radiology that improves categorical radiology decisions over its general-purpose base model and matched or exceeded larger or hosted alternatives.
clinical_relevance: Because it can run inside a hospital and keep data local, RadKev could support faster, privacy-preserving radiology triage and decision support after local validation.
method: Fine-tuned Kev-27B and Kev-9B on 36,109 public radiology records to create RadKev-27B and RadKev-9B.
Compared against base Kev models, hosted decision models, and Qwen3.8-27B on 14,142 held-out questions across 15 radiology tasks.
Evaluated accuracy and latency, with task-averaged accuracy as the prespecified primary outcome.
evidence_signal: RadKev-27B improved over Kev-27B by 4.9 percentage points and was more accurate than Jev, OpenAI Decisions, and Qwen3.8-27B, while running about 132 times faster than reasoning mode on a 1,675-question comparison set.
watch_item: Performance was shown on held-out public datasets, so real-world deployment still needs validation on local workflows, scanner populations, and reporting practices.
paper_title: RadKev: An Open-Weight Decision Model for Radiology
